messages:
maria: seeing a spike of apiserver 5xxs in eu-west1 after a large GPU scale-down window. controller-manager is queuing reconciles, leader-election timeouts showing up. logs look like a burst of kube-proxy conn churn + nat port exhaustion from node churn.

jon: ugh, is this the preemptible deprovision event we expected? any obvious eviction floods?

maria: yes, looks tied to the preemptible GPU pool reclaim around 03:10UTC. many pods moved off at once -> lots of conn resets. snippet from apiserver error stream:```E0310 03:10:12.345678 1 handler.go:152] apiserver error: 503 Service Unavailable: client closed connection / watch stream closed due to EOF```

alex: can you paste `kubectl get events -A --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n50` output? I want to confirm mass pod deletions vs kubelet flapping.

maria: pasted the last 30 lines in thread: `Node gpu-preempt-7 terminated by provider`, `Pod eviction: NodeNotReady`, `kube-proxy: conntrack entries overflow` etc.

priya: cost note: this pool is spot-backed because it's cheap, but if we keep seeing controlplane pain we might need to reserve a small buffer of non-preemptible GPUs in region. that increases monthly committed spend.

jon: short-term mitigations? can we slow the autoscaler or stagger drain?

alex: yes — two quick actions: 1) throttle node pool scale-down to X nodes/min (ASG/autoscaler flag) to reduce blast radius, 2) apply a temporary conntrack tuning on kube-proxy nodes:```sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144``` and bump conntrack hashsize. That should buy us time.

maria: doing conntrack bump now on a few hosts. also toggled cluster-autoscaler --scale-down-unneeded-time to 30m -> will reduce aggressive drains.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-0453, assigned to eng-sre. severity: S2. link: https://redwood.company/incidents/INC-2024-0453 :rotating_light:

priya: longer-term: evaluate a small dedicated GPU reserve (2-4 nodes) per region for HA-critical workloads + increase apiserver max-inflight settings to reduce 503s under reconnect storms. tradeoff = baseline cost vs fewer outages.

jon: devops task: add rollout to node-provisioner to spread preemptible drain windows over 15m. also add autoscaler profiling to detect scale-down storms and circuit-break.

alex: config changes to consider for apiserver/controller-manager: `--max-requests-inflight=300 --min-request-timeout=30s` and controller-manager leader-election retry backoff increased. also check apiserver file descriptor soft limits on controlplane hosts (we saw fd>saturation warnings).

maria: agreed. I'm going to: 1) push conntrack sysctl to daemonset (kube-proxy nodes), 2) patch autoscaler settings, 3) open a PR to add a tiny reserved GPU pool proposal for eu-west1. will update INC-2024-0453 with timeline.

priya: please include cost delta in PR (monthly + one-time infra churn). ops finance wants the estimate before greenlight.

jon: once conntrack bump is in place, keep an eye on apiserver 5xx rate and leader-election logs for 15m. if still noisy, failover traffic to eu-central fallback region for critical workloads.

maria: monitoring: added temporary alert: apiserver_5xx_rate > 10r/m for 5m -> page oncall. also added leader_election_timeout rate alert.

alex: nice. file followups: PR for reserved pool, runbook update for preemptible scale-down blast, and a postmortem if we hit >10min SLI degradation.

maria: thanks all — will update thread and incident.

sre-bot: Note: deployment event recorded: conntrack-daemonset.v1 applied by maria at 03:28UTC.
